limitations: Stories describe documented sites and dedications; they have not been matched to individual inventory TREEIDs.
Dedication years do not establish the ages or present survival of the trees.
Landmark locations include private property and groups; designation does not mean public access.
The official landmark map has 25 points. The Public Works list has 26 entries and is not identical. The map still includes two trees the list records as removed.

stories.title: Mary Ellen Pleasant's living legacy
stories.location: Octavia Street at Bush Street / 1801 Bush Street
stories.text: The landmark blue gums stand at the site of Mary Ellen Pleasant's former home. San Francisco Environment identifies them as trees she planted and celebrated their designation in 2008, connecting the grove with her civil-rights legacy.

programTimeline.title: Landmark Tree Program codified
programTimeline.text: The city formalized protection for exceptional trees under Public Works Code Article 16, Section 810.

programTimeline.title: Voters approve Proposition E
programTimeline.text: Voters authorized a dedicated maintenance program and transfer of street-tree care to Public Works.

programTimeline.title: StreetTreeSF begins
programTimeline.text: Citywide maintenance responsibility transfers to Public Works.
